name: George Miller
role: Nauvoo bishop and Nauvoo House trustee
dateNote: He was baptized in August 1839 and appointed a bishop by section 124 on 19 January 1841.
importance: Section 124 calls him “without guile” and gives him the office of a bishopric like Edward Partridge’s. It also names him first among the men to build the Nauvoo House, a boarding house for visitors. He led the 1842–1843 expedition to the Wisconsin pineries for temple and Nauvoo House lumber. He later broke with Brigham Young and was excommunicated in 1848.
connections: He worked with Lyman Wight, John Snider, and Peter Haws on the Nauvoo House. He later associated with Lyman Wight’s group and then James Strang’s followers.
reviewNote: Birth (25 November 1794, Virginia), baptism (August 1839 by John Taylor), bishopric, Nauvoo House, pinery, 1848 excommunication, and later affiliations checked on JSP. JSP gives his death only as after July 1856, at Marengo, Illinois. Bare “George” in 124:22 is not linked.
